---
title: "Q4 simple"
format: html
---
1. Data preparation
BBL ball-by-ball data (2011/12 to 2024/25), restricted to innings 1 and 2.
Shortened matches excluded, because required runs and balls remaining are distorted in rain-affected games.
Death overs defined as overs 17-20, following the project brief.
Two outcomes per delivery: runs conceded by the bowler (runs off the bat plus wides and no-balls) and bowler wicket (dismissals credited to the bowler, so run-outs are excluded).

```{r}
library(tidyverse); library(lme4); library(here); library(ggrepel)

bbl_all <- readRDS(here("Pranav", "data", "bbl_t20_data.rds")) |> ungroup()

death <- bbl_all |>
  filter(innings %in% c(1, 2), shortened_match == 0, over_no >= 17) |>
  mutate(
    bowler_runs  = runs_off_bat + coalesce(wides, 0) + coalesce(noballs, 0),
    chase        = as.integer(innings == 2),
    req_rr       = if_else(chase == 1,
                           required_runs / pmax(balls_remaining, 1) * 6, 0),
    wickets_lost = pmin(wickets_lost_before, 8)
  )
```

3. Models
A linear mixed model for runs and a logistic mixed model for wickets, with the same predictors in both.
Random effects for bowler, striker and venue. The striker and venue terms mean a bowler isn’t credited for facing tail-enders or bowling at small grounds.
The wicket model uses nAGQ = 0, a faster approximation to the likelihood, to cope with the data size.

4. Why mixed models
Each bowler’s effect is estimated with partial pooling: pulled toward the league average in proportion to how little data he has. This stops a bowler with a lucky 20-over sample from topping the ranking.
Everything is estimated jointly, so the bowler effect is already adjusted for match state, batter and venue.

```{r}
runs_model <- lmer(
  bowler_runs ~ chase * req_rr + wickets_lost + over_no + free_hit +
    (1 | bowler) + (1 | striker) + (1 | venue),
  data = death
)

wicket_model <- glmer(
  bowler_wicket ~ chase * req_rr + wickets_lost + over_no + free_hit +
    (1 | bowler) + (1 | striker) + (1 | venue),
  data = death, family = binomial, nAGQ = 0
)

VarCorr(runs_model); VarCorr(wicket_model)
```

5. Extracting bowler results
Runs saved per over = −(bowler effect) × 6. Positive means fewer runs than an average bowler in the same situations.
Wicket odds ratio = exp(bowler effect). 1.00 is average, and 1.10 means 10% higher odds of a wicket on a ball.
Bowlers need at least 120 legal balls (20 death overs) to be included.

```{r}
runs_effect <- ranef(runs_model)$bowler |>
  rownames_to_column("bowler") |>
  rename(run_effect = `(Intercept)`) |>
  mutate(runs_saved_per_over = -run_effect * 6)

wicket_effect <- ranef(wicket_model)$bowler |>
  rownames_to_column("bowler") |>
  rename(wicket_effect = `(Intercept)`) |>
  mutate(wicket_odds_ratio = exp(wicket_effect))

volume <- death |>
  group_by(bowler) |>
  summarise(legal_balls = sum(legal_ball), overs = legal_balls / 6, .groups = "drop")

bowler_results <- runs_effect |>
  left_join(wicket_effect, by = "bowler") |>
  left_join(volume, by = "bowler") |>
  filter(legal_balls >= 120)

bowler_results |>
  arrange(desc(runs_saved_per_over)) |>
  select(bowler, overs, runs_saved_per_over, wicket_odds_ratio) |>
  mutate(across(where(is.numeric), ~ round(.x, 2))) |>
  head(15)
```


scatter plot

```{r}
plot_data <- bowler_results |>
  mutate(
    top_runs  = min_rank(desc(runs_saved_per_over)) <= 8,
    extreme_w = min_rank(desc(wicket_odds_ratio)) <= 3 |
                min_rank(wicket_odds_ratio) <= 3,
    standout  = top_runs | extreme_w,
    label     = if_else(standout, bowler, NA_character_)
  )

ggplot(plot_data, aes(runs_saved_per_over, wicket_odds_ratio)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 1, linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey60") +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey60") +
  geom_point(aes(colour = standout, size = overs), alpha = 0.7) +
  geom_text_repel(aes(label = label), size = 3, max.overlaps = Inf,
                  box.padding = 0.5, na.rm = TRUE) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c("FALSE" = "grey70", "TRUE" = "#D55E00"), guide = "none") +
  scale_size_continuous(range = c(2, 7), name = "Death overs bowled") +
  labs(x = "Runs saved per over vs average bowler (right = better)",
       y = "Wicket-taking odds ratio (up = better, 1 = average)",
       title = "BBL death-over bowlers (overs 17-20)",
       subtitle = "Adjusted for match state, batter and venue. Bowlers with at least 20 death overs.") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom", panel.grid.minor = element_blank())
```

expeted vs real plot


```{r}
death <- death |>
  mutate(exp_runs = predict(runs_model, re.form = ~ (1 | striker) + (1 | venue)))


rate_tbl <- death |>
  group_by(bowler) |>
  summarise(legal_balls = sum(legal_ball),
            overs       = legal_balls / 6,
            expected    = sum(exp_runs)    / legal_balls * 6,
            actual      = sum(bowler_runs) / legal_balls * 6,
            .groups = "drop") |>
  filter(legal_balls >= 120) |>
  mutate(gap = expected - actual)

plot_lead <- rate_tbl |>
  inner_join(select(bowler_results, bowler, runs_saved_per_over), by = "bowler") |>
  slice_max(runs_saved_per_over, n = 12) |>          # shrunk leaders, same as scatter
  mutate(label = paste0(bowler, " (", sprintf("%.2f", runs_saved_per_over), ")"),
         label = fct_reorder(label, runs_saved_per_over))   # best at top

ggplot(plot_lead, aes(y = label)) +
  geom_segment(aes(x = expected, xend = actual, yend = label), colour = "grey70") +
  geom_point(aes(x = expected, colour = "Model baseline (average bowler)"), size = 3) +
  geom_point(aes(x = actual,   colour = "Actual"), size = 3) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c("Model baseline (average bowler)" = "grey40",
                                 "Actual" = "#D55E00"), name = NULL) +
  labs(x = "Runs per over in the death overs", y = NULL,
       title = "Top death bowlers: actual vs model baseline",
       subtitle = "Ranked by adjusted runs saved per over (in brackets). Baseline = average bowler in the same situations") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) + theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```


```{r}
# Larger text for slides
slide_theme <- theme_minimal(base_size = 16) +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom", panel.grid.minor = element_blank())

q4_scatter <- ggplot(plot_data, aes(runs_saved_per_over, wicket_odds_ratio)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 1, linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey60") +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey60") +
  geom_point(aes(colour = standout, size = overs), alpha = 0.7) +
  geom_text_repel(aes(label = label), size = 4.5, max.overlaps = Inf,
                  box.padding = 0.5, na.rm = TRUE) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c("FALSE" = "grey70", "TRUE" = "#D55E00"), guide = "none") +
  scale_size_continuous(range = c(2, 7), name = "Death overs bowled") +
  labs(x = "Runs saved per over vs average bowler (right = better)",
       y = "Wicket odds ratio (up = better)",
       title = "BBL death-over bowlers (overs 17-20)") +
  slide_theme

q4_baseline <- ggplot(plot_lead, aes(y = label)) +
  geom_segment(aes(x = expected, xend = actual, yend = label), colour = "grey70") +
  geom_point(aes(x = expected, colour = "Model baseline"), size = 3) +
  geom_point(aes(x = actual, colour = "Actual"), size = 3) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c("Model baseline" = "grey40", "Actual" = "#D55E00"),
                      name = NULL) +
  labs(x = "Runs per over in the death overs", y = NULL,
       title = "Top run-restricting death bowlers", subtitle = "Ranked by adjusted runs saved per over.") +
  slide_theme

vc <- function(m) as.data.frame(VarCorr(m)) |> select(group = grp, sd = sdcor)

q4_objects <- list(
  plots = list(scatter = q4_scatter, baseline = q4_baseline),
  tables = list(top10 = bowler_results |>
                  arrange(desc(runs_saved_per_over)) |>
                  select(bowler, overs, runs_saved_per_over, wicket_odds_ratio) |>
                  head(10)),
  numbers = list(n_bowlers = nrow(bowler_results),
                 runs_sd = vc(runs_model), wicket_sd = vc(wicket_model),
                 or_range = range(bowler_results$wicket_odds_ratio),
                 runs_range = range(bowler_results$runs_saved_per_over))
)

sd_bars <- vc(runs_model) |>
  filter(group != "Residual") |>
  mutate(runs_per_over = sd * 6,
         group = recode(group, striker = "Batter", bowler = "Bowler", venue = "Venue")) |>
  ggplot(aes(reorder(group, runs_per_over), runs_per_over)) +
  geom_col(fill = "#D55E00") + coord_flip() +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Spread in effect (runs per over)",
       title = "Who moves death-over scoring?") +
  slide_theme

q4_objects$plots$sd_bars <- sd_bars
death <- death |>
  mutate(exp_wkt = predict(wicket_model, type = "response",
                           re.form = ~ (1 | striker) + (1 | venue)))

wkt_tbl <- death |>
  group_by(bowler) |>
  summarise(legal_balls = sum(legal_ball),
            expected = sum(exp_wkt)       / legal_balls * 6,
            actual   = sum(bowler_wicket) / legal_balls * 6,
            .groups = "drop") |>
  filter(legal_balls >= 120)

plot_wkt <- wkt_tbl |>
  inner_join(select(bowler_results, bowler, wicket_odds_ratio), by = "bowler") |>
  slice_max(wicket_odds_ratio, n = 12) |>
  mutate(label = paste0(bowler, " (", sprintf("%.2f", wicket_odds_ratio), ")"),
         label = fct_reorder(label, wicket_odds_ratio))

q4_wkt_baseline <- ggplot(plot_wkt, aes(y = label)) +
  geom_segment(aes(x = expected, xend = actual, yend = label), colour = "grey70") +
  geom_point(aes(x = expected, colour = "Model baseline (average bowler)"), size = 3) +
  geom_point(aes(x = actual,   colour = "Actual"), size = 3) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c("Model baseline (average bowler)" = "grey40",
                                 "Actual" = "#D55E00"), name = NULL) +
  labs(x = "Wickets per over in the death overs", y = NULL,
       title = "Top wicket-taking death bowlers",
       subtitle = "Ranked by adjusted wicket odds ratio") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 16) +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")

q4_wkt_baseline

q4_objects$plots$wkt_baseline <- q4_wkt_baseline


saveRDS(q4_objects, here("Pranav", "data", "q4_presentation_objects.rds"))

```
